title: Lira Roadmap: Next Milestones
content:
# Lira Roadmap: Next Milestones

Based on the current state (Phases 0-8 mostly complete), here are 20 suggested milestones organized into future phases.

---

## Phase 9: Developer Experience & Debugging

| ID    | Task                    | Description                                                              |
| ----- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| T9.1  | **REPL**                | Interactive interpreter for quick experimentation (`lira repl`)          |
| T9.2  | **AST Dump Flag**       | `lirac --ast file.li` to output parsed AST as JSON/pretty-print          |
| T9.3  | **Bytecode Disassembler** | `lirac --disasm file.lic` for human-readable bytecode inspection       |
| T9.4  | **Debug Symbols**       | Emit DWARF-like debug info, source mapping for stack traces              |
| T9.5  | **Step Debugger**       | Interactive debugger with breakpoints, step-in/over, variable inspection |

---

## Phase 10: Performance & Profiling

| ID     | Task                      | Description                                                          |
| ------ | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| T10.1  | **Benchmark Suite**       | Standardized benchmarks (fibonacci, primes, sorting, I/O, fibers)    |
| T10.2  | **Cross-Language Benchmarks** | Compare against Go, Rust, Python, Lua, JavaScript, Ruby           |
| T10.3  | **Runtime Profiler**      | CPU time profiling with flame graphs (`liravm --profile`)            |
| T10.4  | **Memory Profiler**       | Heap allocation tracking, leak detection, ARC cycle analysis         |
| T10.5  | **Code Coverage**         | Test coverage reports with line-level granularity                    |

---

## Phase 11: Package Ecosystem

| ID     | Task                    | Description                                                            |
| ------ | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| T11.1  | **Package Manifest**    | `lira.toml` for project metadata, dependencies, build config          |
| T11.2  | **Package Manager**     | `lira add`, `lira install`, dependency resolution (like cargo/npm)    |
| T11.3  | **Package Registry**    | Central registry for publishing/discovering packages                   |
| T11.4  | **Build System**        | `lira build`, `lira test`, `lira run` unified CLI                     |

---

## Phase 12: Native Compilation

| ID     | Task                      | Description                                                          |
| ------ | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| T12.1  | **LLVM Backend**          | Compile Lira AST → LLVM IR → native machine code                     |
| T12.2  | **Native Binary Output**  | Produce standalone executables (no VM required)                      |
| T12.3  | **Cross-Compilation**     | Target different architectures (x86_64, ARM64, WASM)                 |
| T12.4  | **WebAssembly Target**    | Compile to WASM for browser/edge deployment                          |

---

## Phase 13: Interoperability

| ID     | Task                    | Description                                                            |
| ------ | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| T13.1  | **C FFI**               | Call C libraries, define extern functions, handle ABI                  |
| T13.2  | **Embedded Runtime**    | Embed Lira VM in Rust/C applications as a scripting engine            |
| T13.3  | **Async I/O**           | Non-blocking I/O integrated with fiber scheduler (io_uring/kqueue)    |

---

## Phase 14: Self-Hosting

| ID     | Task                      | Description                                                          |
| ------ | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| T14.1  | **Self-Hosted Compiler**  | Rewrite lirac in Lira itself (bootstrap compiler)                    |
| T14.2  | **Self-Hosted VM**        | Rewrite liravm in Lira (optional, significant undertaking)           |

---

## Phase 15: Advanced Language Features

| ID     | Task                    | Description                                                            |
| ------ | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| T15.1  | **Macro System**        | Compile-time metaprogramming (hygenic macros or proc-macros)          |
| T15.2  | **Comptime Evaluation** | Compile-time function execution (`const fn` / `comptime`)             |
| T15.3  | **Effect System**       | Track side effects in type system (IO, exceptions, etc.)              |

---

## Bonus: Community & Ecosystem

| ID     | Task                    | Description                                                            |
| ------ | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| T16.1  | **Online Playground**   | Web-based REPL (like Go Playground, Rust Playground)                  |
| T16.2  | **Language Tutorial**   | Interactive "Tour of Lira" guide                                       |
| T16.3  | **Static Analyzer**     | Linter with configurable rules (`lira lint`)                          |
| T16.4  | **JIT Compilation**     | Hot-path optimization with tracing JIT                                 |

---

## Suggested Priority Order

1. **Immediate wins** (Phase 9): REPL, AST dump, disassembler — low effort, high developer value
2. **Validation** (Phase 10): Benchmarks to prove/improve performance
3. **Ecosystem** (Phase 11): Package manager enables community growth
4. **Native path** (Phase 12): LLVM backend for production-grade performance
5. **Integration** (Phase 13): FFI opens entire C ecosystem
6. **Maturity** (Phase 14): Self-hosting proves the language

---

## Quick Reference: Top 20

1. REPL

4. Debug Symbols
5. Step Debugger
6. Benchmark Suite
7. Cross-Language Benchmarks
8. Runtime Profiler

title: Rename Li-lang to Lira
content:
# Rename Li-lang to Lira

## Summary

Rename the language from "Li-lang" to "Lira" while keeping:
- `.li` source file extension
- `.lic` bytecode extension (now "Lira Compiled")

## New Naming Scheme

| Old | New | Notes |
|-----|-----|-------|
| Li-lang | Lira | Language name |
| li-common | lira-core | Core types and opcodes |
| lic | lirac | Lira Compiler |
| livm | liravm | Lira Virtual Machine |
| LIUI | Lira UI | UI format (keep `.liui` extension) |
| .li | .li | Keep as-is |
| .lic | .lic | Keep as-is (Lira Compiled) |

## Improved Package Structure

```
lira/
├── crates/
│   ├── lira-core/       # Shared types, opcodes, bytecode format
│   ├── lirac/           # Compiler (lexer, parser, checker, codegen)
│   ├── liravm/          # Virtual machine runtime
│   ├── lira-lsp/        # Language Server Protocol (future)
│   └── lira-fmt/        # Code formatter (future)
├── editors/
│   ├── tree-sitter-lira/    # Tree-sitter grammar
│   ├── vscode-lira/         # VS Code extension
│   └── jetbrains-lira/      # JetBrains plugin
├── stdlib/              # Standard library (.li files)
├── examples/            # Example programs
├── docs/                # Documentation
└── tests/               # Integration tests
```

### Package Descriptions

| Package | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `lira-core` | Opcodes, bytecode format, shared types between compiler and VM |
| `lirac` | Compiler: lexer, parser, type checker, code generator |
| `liravm` | VM: bytecode interpreter, fiber scheduler, runtime |
| `lira-lsp` | LSP server for IDE integration (future) |
| `lira-fmt` | Code formatter like `rustfmt` (future) |
| `tree-sitter-lira` | Tree-sitter grammar for syntax highlighting |
| `vscode-lira` | VS Code / compatible editors extension |
| `jetbrains-lira` | IntelliJ / JetBrains IDE plugin |

## Changes Required

### 1. Directory Restructure
```
# Create new structure
mkdir -p crates editors

# Move and rename packages
mv li-common crates/lira-core
mv lic crates/lirac
mv livm crates/liravm

# Create editor package placeholders (for future)
mkdir -p editors/tree-sitter-lira
mkdir -p editors/vscode-lira
mkdir -p editors/jetbrains-lira
```

### 2. Cargo Configuration

**Root Cargo.toml:**
```toml
[workspace]
members = ["crates/lira-core", "crates/lirac", "crates/liravm"]
```

**crates/lira-core/Cargo.toml:**
- Package name: `lira-core`
- Description: "Core types and opcodes for Lira"

**crates/lirac/Cargo.toml:**
- Package name: `lirac`
- Binary name: `lirac`
- Library name: `lirac`
- Description: "Lira compiler"
- Dependency: `lira-core = { path = "../lira-core" }`

**crates/liravm/Cargo.toml:**
- Package name: `liravm`
- Binary name: `liravm`
- Library name: `liravm`
- Description: "Lira Virtual Machine"
- Dependency: `lira-core = { path = "../lira-core" }`

### 3. Justfile Commands
Simplify to unprefixed commands:
- `li-build` → `build`
- `li-test` → `test`
- `li-run` → `run`
- `li-check` → `check`
- `li-clippy` → `clippy`
- Package references: `--package lirac --package liravm --package lira-core`
- Binary paths: `./target/release/lirac`, `./target/release/liravm`

### 4. Root Directory Rename
```bash
# Rename project directory
mv /Users/helge/code/li-lang /Users/helge/code/lira
```

### 5. Source Code Updates

**crates/lirac/src/*.rs** (7 files):
- Module doc comments: "Li-lang" → "Lira"
- Help text and version strings
- Example comments

**crates/liravm/src/*.rs** (7 files):
- Module doc comments: "Li-lang" → "Lira"
- Help text and version strings

**crates/lira-core/src/*.rs**:
- Module doc comments

### 6. Documentation Updates

**README.md:**
- Title and description
- Project structure diagram
- All tool references
- Example commands

**docs/*.md** (14 files):
- Titles and headers
- All "Li-lang" references → "Lira"
- "LIUI" → "Lira UI" (keep `.liui` extension)
- Tool references (lic → lirac, livm → liravm)

### 7. Example/Test Files
- Update comments in example `.li` files
- Update `tests/samples/hello.li` comment

## Execution Order

1. Rename root directory: `li-lang/` → `lira/`
2. Create `crates/` and `editors/` directories
3. Move and rename packages into `crates/`
4. Update all Cargo.toml files
5. Update justfile with new paths and simplified commands
6. Update source code comments/strings
7. Update README.md
8. Update all docs/*.md files
9. Update example file comments
10. Run `cargo build` to verify
11. Delete Cargo.lock (will be regenerated)
12. Clean target/ directory

## Files to Modify

### Critical Files
- `Cargo.toml` (root workspace)
- `crates/lirac/Cargo.toml`
- `crates/liravm/Cargo.toml`
- `crates/lira-core/Cargo.toml`
- `justfile`
- `README.md`

### Source Files (after restructure)
- `crates/lirac/src/main.rs`
- `crates/lirac/src/lib.rs`
- `crates/lirac/src/lexer.rs`
- `crates/lirac/src/parser.rs`
- `crates/lirac/src/ast.rs`
- `crates/lirac/src/module_loader.rs`
- `crates/liravm/src/main.rs`
- `crates/liravm/src/lib.rs`
- `crates/liravm/src/vm.rs`
- `crates/liravm/src/runtime.rs`
- `crates/liravm/src/fiber.rs`
- `crates/liravm/src/memory.rs`
- `crates/liravm/src/value.rs`
- `crates/lira-core/src/lib.rs`

### Documentation Files
- `docs/00-li-lang-overview.md` → rename to `docs/00-lira-overview.md`
- `docs/ROADMAP.md`
- `docs/01-lexical-structure.md`
- `docs/02-type-system.md`
- `docs/03-syntax-constructs.md`
- `docs/04-concurrency.md`
- `docs/05-module-system.md`
- `docs/10-bytecode-format.md`
- `docs/11-instruction-set.md`
- `docs/12-vm-runtime.md`
- `docs/13-memory-model.md`
- `docs/20-liui-format.md`
- `docs/21-liui-widgets.md`
- `docs/30-standard-library.md`
- `docs/40-compiler-architecture.md`
- `docs/50-tooling.md`
- `docs/51-testing.md`

## Estimated Changes
- ~350+ string replacements
- 3 directory renames + restructure to crates/
- 4 Cargo.toml updates
- 1 justfile update
- ~14 source files
- ~17 documentation files

---

## Future Tooling Roadmap

### Phase 1: Tree-sitter Grammar (editors/tree-sitter-lira/)
Create tree-sitter grammar for syntax highlighting in all modern editors.

```
editors/tree-sitter-lira/
├── grammar.js           # Grammar definition
├── src/
│   ├── scanner.c        # External scanner (if needed)
│   └── parser.c         # Generated parser
├── queries/
│   ├── highlights.scm   # Syntax highlighting queries
│   ├── injections.scm   # Language injection rules
│   ├── locals.scm       # Local variable tracking
│   └── folds.scm        # Code folding rules
├── bindings/
│   ├── node/            # Node.js bindings
│   └── rust/            # Rust bindings
├── package.json
└── Cargo.toml
```

**Key highlights.scm categories:**
- Keywords: `fn`, `let`, `var`, `if`, `else`, `match`, `spawn`, etc.
- Types: `int`, `float`, `bool`, `string`, `struct`, `enum`
- Operators: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `=>`, `->`, etc.
- Comments: `//`, `/* */`
- Strings and interpolation
- Function definitions and calls

### Phase 2: LSP Server (crates/lira-lsp/)
Language Server Protocol implementation for IDE features.

```
crates/lira-lsp/
├── Cargo.toml
└── src/
    ├── main.rs          # LSP server entry point
    ├── capabilities.rs  # Supported LSP features
    ├── diagnostics.rs   # Error/warning reporting
    ├── completion.rs    # Auto-completion

### Phase 3: VS Code Extension (editors/vscode-lira/)

```
editors/vscode-lira/
├── package.json         # Extension manifest
├── syntaxes/
│   └── lira.tmLanguage.json  # TextMate grammar (fallback)

```

**Features:**
- Syntax highlighting (via tree-sitter or TextMate)

### Phase 4: JetBrains Plugin (editors/jetbrains-lira/)

```

│   ├── kotlin/

# Fuzzing Infrastructure Migration Plan

## Summary

Replace AFL++ standalone harnesses with Zig's native `--fuzz` coverage-guided fuzzing. Remove old harness files and add inline fuzz tests using `std.testing.fuzzInput`.

---

## Phase 1: Remove Old AFL++ Infrastructure

**Delete these files:**
- `src/fuzz_parse.zig`
- `src/fuzz_lexer.zig`
- `src/fuzz_executor.zig`
- `src/fuzz_glob.zig`
- `scripts/dumb-fuzz.sh`

**Remove from `build.zig`:**
- All `fuzz-parse`, `fuzz-lexer`, `fuzz-executor`, `fuzz-glob` build targets (~70 lines)

**Remove from `Jakefile`:**
- `fuzz` and `fuzz-afl` tasks

**Clean up:**
- Delete `corpus/` directory (Zig fuzzer manages its own corpus)
- Delete `findings/` directory

---

## Phase 2: Add Inline Fuzz Tests

Add `test "fuzz ..."` blocks to source files:

| File | Fuzz Test |
|------|-----------|
| `src/lexer.zig` | Tokenize fuzzed input |
| `src/parser.zig` | Parse fuzzed Jakefile source |
| `src/glob.zig` | Match fuzzed patterns against paths |
| `src/functions.zig` | Evaluate fuzzed function calls |
| `src/conditions.zig` | Evaluate fuzzed condition expressions |

**Example:**
```zig
test "fuzz lexer" {
    const input = std.testing.fuzzInput(.{});
    var lex = Lexer.init(input);
    while (lex.next().tag != .eof) {}
}
```

---

## Phase 3: Update Documentation

Rewrite `docs/FUZZING.md`:
- Remove all AFL++/honggfuzz instructions
- Document new `zig build test --fuzz` workflow
- Explain coverage web UI

---

## Files to Delete

| File | Reason |
|------|--------|
| `src/fuzz_parse.zig` | Replaced by inline test in parser.zig |
| `src/fuzz_lexer.zig` | Replaced by inline test in lexer.zig |
| `src/fuzz_executor.zig` | Replaced by inline test in executor.zig |
| `src/fuzz_glob.zig` | Replaced by inline test in glob.zig |
| `scripts/dumb-fuzz.sh` | No longer needed |

## Files to Modify

| File | Changes |
|------|---------|
| `src/lexer.zig` | Add fuzz test |
| `src/parser.zig` | Add fuzz test |
| `src/glob.zig` | Add fuzz test |
| `src/functions.zig` | Add fuzz test |
| `src/conditions.zig` | Add fuzz test |
| `build.zig` | Remove fuzz-* build targets |
| `Jakefile` | Remove fuzz/fuzz-afl tasks, add new fuzz task |
| `docs/FUZZING.md` | Rewrite for new system |

---

## New Usage

```bash
# Run fuzz tests with coverage guidance
zig build test --fuzz

# Fuzz indefinitely until stopped (Ctrl+C)
zig build test --fuzz --indefinite

# View coverage in web UI
zig build test --fuzz --port 8080
```

---

## Implementation Order

1. Delete old fuzz harness files
2. Remove build targets from `build.zig`
3. Add fuzz test to `src/lexer.zig`
4. Add fuzz test to `src/parser.zig`
5. Add fuzz test to `src/glob.zig`
6. Add fuzz test to `src/functions.zig`
7. Add fuzz test to `src/conditions.zig`
8. Update `Jakefile` with new fuzz task
9. Rewrite `docs/FUZZING.md`
10. Clean up `corpus/` and `findings/` directories

```typescript
function extractProject(content: string): string | null {
  // Match paths like /Users/helge/code/projectname/...
  const pathMatch = content.match(/\/Users\/\w+\/code\/([^\/\s]+)/);
  if (pathMatch) return pathMatch[1];

  // Fallback: match any absolute path with common code dirs
  const altMatch = content.match(/(?:\/[\w-]+)+\/([^\/\s]+)\/(?:src|lib|app|docs)\//);
  if (altMatch) return altMatch[1];

  return null;
}
```

title: Fix Direct URL Navigation Not Loading Tab Data
content:
# Plan: Fix Direct URL Navigation Not Loading Tab Data

## Problem
When navigating directly to `http://localhost:3000/#analytics` (or any tab via hash), the data doesn't load. It only loads when clicking the tab manually.

## Root Cause
`currentTab` is initialized at **script parse time** (line 3):
```javascript
let currentTab = getTabFromHash() || 'timeline';
```

With the `defer` script attribute, there can be a timing issue where `window.location.hash` isn't reliably available when line 3 executes. The hash reading should happen inside `init()` when the DOM is fully ready.

## File to Modify
- `public/app.js`

## Implementation

### Step 1: Move hash reading into `init()`

**Change line 3 from:**
```javascript
let currentTab = getTabFromHash() || 'timeline';
```

**To:**
```javascript
let currentTab = 'timeline';
```

### Step 2: Read hash in `init()` before `showTab()`

**In the `init()` function (around line 98-99), change:**
```javascript
// Load initial tab from hash or default to timeline
showTab(currentTab);
```

**To:**
```javascript
// Load initial tab from hash or default to timeline
currentTab = getTabFromHash() || 'timeline';
showTab(currentTab);
```

This ensures the hash is read after the DOM is fully ready and all setup is complete, but before `showTab()` is called.

## Why This Fixes the Issue
1. The initial `currentTab = 'timeline'` is just a default
2. When `init()` runs (after DOM ready), we read the actual hash from the URL
3. `showTab()` then correctly shows the tab from the URL and loads its data
4. The `hashchange` event listener (lines 109-114) continues to work for back/forward navigation

title: Dogfood Unused Jake Features
content:
# Plan: Dogfood Unused Jake Features

## Jake Features Analysis

### Currently USED in our Jakefile:
- `@import` - ✅ lib/build.jake, lib/release.jake
- `@dotenv` - ✅ Loading .env
- `@default` - ✅ Marking default task
- `@desc` - ✅ Task descriptions
- `@group` - ✅ Task grouping
- `@pre/@post` - ✅ Global and recipe hooks
- `@on_error` - ✅ Global error hook
- `@only-os` - ✅ Platform-specific tasks
- `@quiet` - ✅ In _generate-large-jakefile
- `@needs` - ✅ Checking for commands
- `@each` - ✅ Looping in several tasks
- `@if/@else/@end` - ✅ Conditionals
- `@cd` - ✅ In e2e task
- `@confirm` - ✅ In release.package
- `exists()` - ✅ Path checks
- `eq()` - ✅ String comparison
- `lowercase()` - ✅ In sizes task
- `home()` - ✅ In install task
- `local_bin()` - ✅ In install task
- `is_watching()` - ✅ In dev task

### NOT USED but could be useful:

| Feature | Where to use it | Benefit |
|---------|-----------------|---------|
| `@cache` | `build` task | Skip rebuild if src/*.zig unchanged |
| `@watch` | `dev` task | Explicit watch patterns for `-w` mode |
| `@require` | Global | Require ZIG env var or version check |
| `@alias` | Common tasks | `b` for build, `t` for test |
| `file` targets | Build output | Track zig-out/bin/jake as file target |
| `{{$1}}` positional | Parameterized tasks | `jake run-sample 01-basics` |
| `@export` | Version var | Export VERSION to child processes |
| `@before`/`@after` | Targeted hooks | Before/after specific recipes |
| `uppercase()` | Not applicable | - |
| `dirname()`/`basename()` | Path handling | Could use in complex paths |
| `extension()` | Not applicable | - |
| `env()` condition | Runtime checks | Check for optional env vars |
| `neq()` | Inequality | Alternative conditional |
| `@shell` | Custom shell | Use bash explicitly |
| `@ignore` | Flaky commands | Continue on failure |

## Suggested Changes

### 1. Add `@cache` to build task
```jake
@group build
task build:
    @needs zig
    @cache src/*.zig build.zig  # Skip if sources unchanged
    zig build
```

### 2. Add `@watch` patterns to dev task
```jake
@group dev
task dev:
    @watch src/*.zig build.zig Jakefile
    zig build
```

### 3. Add `@require` for environment validation
```jake
# At top of Jakefile
@require PATH  # Sanity check
# Or in lib/release.jake for releases:
@require GITHUB_TOKEN  # Required for releases
```

### 4. Add `file` target for compiled binary
```jake
# File target: only rebuild if sources newer than output
file zig-out/bin/jake: src/*.zig build.zig
    zig build
```

### 5. Add positional args for flexible tasks
```jake
@group samples
@desc "Run a specific sample (usage: jake run-sample 01-basics)"
task run-sample:
    @if exists(samples/{{$1}}/Jakefile)
        cd samples/{{$1}} && jake
    @else
        echo "Sample not found: {{$1}}"
        echo "Available: 01-basics, 02-parallel, ..."
    @end
```

### 6. Add `@export` for version
```jake
@export version  # Make VERSION available to child processes
```

### 7. Add targeted hooks
```jake
@before release.all echo "Starting cross-platform build..."
@after release.all echo "All platforms built successfully!"
```

### 8. Add `@ignore` for optional cleanup
```jake
task clean:
    @ignore
    rm -rf zig-out .zig-cache .jake dist
    echo "Clean complete"
```

### 9. Use more functions
```jake
task show-paths:
    echo "Home: {{home()}}"
    echo "Shell config: {{shell_config()}}"
    echo "Project: {{absolute_path(.)}}"
    echo "Binary: {{basename(zig-out/bin/jake)}}"
```

## Implementation Priority

**High impact (add these):**
1. `@cache` on build - Speeds up repeated builds
2. `@watch` on dev - Better watch mode UX
3. `file` target - Proper dependency tracking
4. `@ignore` on clean - Don't fail if dirs missing

**Medium impact:**
5. Positional args for samples - More flexible testing
6. `@export version` - Useful for scripts
7. Targeted hooks - Better release feedback

**Low impact (nice to have):**
8. `@require` - Not strictly needed
9. More functions - Demonstrative value only

## Files to Modify
- `Jakefile` - Add @export, targeted hooks
- `lib/build.jake` - Add @cache, @watch, @ignore, file target
- `lib/release.jake` - Add @require GITHUB_TOKEN (optional)

### 2. Code Stats Group (`stats`)
```jake
@group stats
task loc               # Count lines of code (zig files)
task todos             # Find TODO/FIXME/HACK comments
task complexity        # Show largest/most complex files
task deps              # Show module dependency graph
```

### 3. Git/Release Workflow Group (`git`)
```jake
@group git
task changelog         # Generate changelog from commits
task bump              # Bump version (param: major|minor|patch)
task tag               # Create and push git tag
task contributors      # List contributors
```

### 4. Samples/Examples Group (`samples`)
```jake
@group samples
task samples-test      # Run all sample Jakefiles
task samples-validate  # Validate all samples parse correctly
task samples-list      # List all sample projects
```

### 5. Debugging/Inspection Group (`debug`)
```jake
@group debug
task dump-tokens       # Show lexer output for a file
task dump-ast          # Show parsed AST (dry-run verbose)
task trace             # Run with verbose tracing
task compare-just      # Compare output with just (side-by-side)
```

### 6. Maintenance Group (`maint`)
```jake
@group maint
task self-update       # Update installed jake binary
task cache-clean       # Clear jake cache files
task prune             # Remove old build artifacts
```

### 7. Quick Commands (Aliases)
```jake
@alias b               # Alias for build
@alias t               # Alias for test
@alias r               # Alias for rebuild
@alias c               # Alias for clean
```

## User Choices
- **Add all groups:** docs, stats, git, samples, debug, maint
- **No aliases:** Skip single-letter shortcuts

## Tasks to Add

### docs group
- `docs` - `zig build-lib src/root.zig -femit-docs=docs -fno-emit-bin`
- `docs-serve` - Python simple HTTP server on docs/
- `readme-validate` - Extract code blocks and verify they parse

### stats group
- `loc` - `find src -name "*.zig" | xargs wc -l | tail -1`
- `todos` - `grep -rn "TODO\|FIXME\|HACK\|XXX" src/`
- `complexity` - `wc -l src/*.zig | sort -n | tail -10`
- `deps` - Show imports between modules

### git group
- `changelog` - `git log --oneline $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD`
- `bump` - Edit version in main.zig + Jakefile (param: major|minor|patch)
- `tag` - `git tag -a v{{version}} -m "Release {{version}}" && git push --tags`
- `contributors` - `git shortlog -sn`

### samples group
- `samples-test` - Run e2e tests on samples
- `samples-validate` - `@each` sample dir, run `jake -n` to validate parsing
- `samples-list` - List sample directories with descriptions

### debug group
- `dump-tokens` - (requires adding --dump-tokens flag, skip for now)
- `trace` - `jake -v` verbose mode
- `compare-just` - Side-by-side diff with just output

### maint group
- `self-update` - Rebuild and reinstall jake
- `cache-clean` - `rm -rf .jake`
- `prune` - `rm -rf zig-out .zig-cache dist`

## File to Modify
- `Jakefile` - Add all new task groups at the end

title: Rust Log Viewer with Sciter GUI - Implementation Plan
content:
# Rust Log Viewer with Sciter GUI - Implementation Plan

## Overview
Build a high-performance log viewer for multi-GB files using Rust, Sciter GUI, memory-mapped I/O, and real-time tailing.

**Target Directory**: `rust-log-viewer/`

## Architecture Summary

### Threading Model
- **Main Thread**: Sciter GUI event loop (must stay unblocked)
- **File Watcher Thread**: Tokio async runtime monitoring file changes
- **Parser Thread**: Background parsing/filtering

### Data Flow
```
File → memmap2 (Arc<Mmap>) → LineIterator → Parser → Filter/Colorize → GUI
                      ↓
               File Watcher (notify) → New Lines → GUI Update
```

### Key Technologies
- **GUI**: sciter-rs (HTML/CSS/TIScript interface)
- **CLI**: clap with derive macros
- **Memory Mapping**: memmap2 (zero-copy, 99.4% memory reduction)
- **File Watching**: notify + tokio (cross-platform FS events)
- **Search**: regex crate

## Critical Files to Implement

### 1. Core File Handling
**`src/file/line_iterator.rs`**
- Iterator over `&[u8]` from memory-mapped file
- Find line boundaries (\n, \r\n)
- Window-based iteration (start_offset, end_offset) for large files
- Use `memchr` crate for SIMD-accelerated newline search

**`src/file/mmap.rs`**
- `MmapFile` struct wrapping `Arc<Mmap>`
- `open()` method with error handling
- Thread-safe shared access pattern

**`src/file/watcher.rs`**
- Use `notify::recommended_watcher()` for FS events
- Watch for WRITE and TRUNCATE events
- Remap file on growth, send new lines to GUI
- Handle file rotation gracefully

### 2. Application State
**`src/state/app_state.rs`**
- `Arc<Mutex<AppState>>` for thread-safe shared state
- Fields: `Arc<Mmap>`, current_offset, total_lines, active_filter, follow_mode
- `get_lines(start, count)` method for range queries

**`src/state/message.rs`**
- `GuiMessage` enum: NewLines, FileGrew, SearchResults, Error
- `WatcherMessage` enum: FileChanged, FileMoved, Error
- Message passing between threads via mpsc channels

### 3. Parsing & Display
**`src/parser/log_line.rs`**
- `LogLine` struct: timestamp, level, message, raw bytes
- Auto-detect format (JSON, syslog, Laravel, plain text)
- Parse common patterns with regex

**`src/parser/colorizer.rs`**
- Color schemes by log level (ERROR=red, WARN=yellow, INFO=green)
- Generate HTML `<span>` tags with CSS classes for Sciter
- Highlight keywords: stack traces, IPs, URLs, errors

**`src/parser/filter.rs`**
- Regex-based text search on raw bytes (fastest)
- Log level filtering
- Time range filtering
- Incremental search: visible window first, background scan remainder

### 4. GUI Layer
**`src/gui/resources.html`**
- HTML structure: header (search input, filter dropdown), log container, status bar
- CSS: Dark theme, monospace font, syntax colors
- TIScript: Event handlers, DOM manipulation
- Virtual scrolling: render visible lines only
- Keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl+F search, follow mode toggle

**`src/gui/window.rs`**
- Initialize Sciter window with Builder pattern
- Embed `resources.html` using `include_bytes!`
- Window config: 1200x800, resizable, title "Rust Log Viewer"
- Handle window lifecycle events

**`src/gui/handlers.rs`**
- Implement `EventHandler` trait with `dispatch_script_call!`
- Methods callable from JavaScript:
  - `load_lines(start: u64, count: u64) -> Vec<Value>`
  - `search(query: String) -> Value`
  - `set_filter(level: String) -> Value`
  - `toggle_follow() -> Value`
- DOM updates: append lines, update status bar, highlight matches

### 5. CLI & Main
**`src/cli.rs`**
- `CliArgs` struct with clap derives
- Arguments: file_path (required), --follow, --filter, --no-color, --tail-lines
- Convert to `Config` struct with validation

**`src/main.rs`**
- Parse CLI args → create Config
- Initialize mmap from file path
- Create `Arc<AppState>`
- Spawn file watcher thread (tokio runtime)
- Spawn parser thread
- Create Sciter window with event handler
- Message pump: receive from parser, call Sciter DOM updates
- Run Sciter event loop (`frame.run_app()`)

## Project Structure
```
rust-log-viewer/
├── Cargo.toml
├── src/
│   ├── main.rs
│   ├── cli.rs
│   ├── config.rs
│   ├── file/
│   │   ├── mod.rs
│   │   ├── mmap.rs
│   │   ├── watcher.rs
│   │   └── line_iterator.rs
│   ├── parser/
│   │   ├── mod.rs
│   │   ├── log_line.rs
│   │   ├── colorizer.rs
│   │   └── filter.rs
│   ├── state/
│   │   ├── mod.rs
│   │   ├── app_state.rs
│   │   └── message.rs
│   └── gui/
│       ├── mod.rs
│       ├── window.rs
│       ├── handlers.rs
│       └── resources.html
├── tests/
│   └── integration_test.rs
└── benches/
    └── mmap_benchmark.rs
```

## Cargo.toml Dependencies
```toml
[dependencies]
sciter-rs = "0.5.58"
clap = { version = "4.4", features = ["derive"] }
memmap2 = "0.9"
notify = "6.1"
tokio = { version = "1.35", features = ["rt", "sync", "fs", "macros"] }
regex = "1.10"
lazy_static = "1.4"
serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0"
anyhow = "1.0"
thiserror = "1.0"
log = "0.4"
env_logger = "0.11"
memchr = "2.7"  # SIMD newline search optimization

[dev-dependencies]
criterion = "0.5"
tempfile = "3.8"
```

## Implementation Steps

### Phase 1: Project Setup
1. `cargo new rust-log-viewer`
2. Update `Cargo.toml` with dependencies
3. Create directory structure (file/, parser/, state/, gui/)
4. Download Sciter SDK and add to PATH

### Phase 2: Core File Layer (Bottom-Up)
5. Implement `file/line_iterator.rs` - Iterator over byte slices
6. Implement `file/mmap.rs` - Memory-mapped file wrapper
7. Write tests with `/var/log/install.log` (16MB test file)
8. Implement `file/watcher.rs` - File monitoring with notify

### Phase 3: Parsing & State
9. Implement `state/message.rs` - Message enums
10. Implement `state/app_state.rs` - Thread-safe shared state
11. Implement `parser/log_line.rs` - Log parsing with format detection
12. Implement `parser/colorizer.rs` - HTML generation with syntax colors
13. Implement `parser/filter.rs` - Search and filtering logic

### Phase 4: CLI
14. Implement `cli.rs` - Clap argument parsing
15. Implement `config.rs` - Configuration struct

### Phase 5: GUI Integration
16. Implement `gui/resources.html` - UI layout and TIScript
17. Implement `gui/window.rs` - Sciter window initialization
18. Implement `gui/handlers.rs` - Event handlers bridging Rust ↔ JavaScript

### Phase 6: Main Integration
19. Implement `main.rs` - Wire all components together
20. Test with `/var/log/install.log`
21. Test tail mode with growing file (use `echo >> test.log`)

### Phase 7: Testing & Polish
22. Write integration tests
23. Add benchmarks for performance validation
24. Error handling and user feedback
25. README with build instructions

## Test Files Available
- `/var/log/install.log` - 16MB Apple system log (primary test file)
- `/Users/helge/code/craft/storage/logs/web-2025-03-08.log` - 3.3MB Laravel log
- Generate large files: `for i in {1..1000000}; do echo "2025-01-07 $(date +%H:%M:%S) INFO Test log line $i" >> large.log; done`

## Key Design Decisions

### Virtual Scrolling
Only render visible lines in GUI (calculate from scroll position). Constant memory regardless of file size.

### Incremental Search
1. Search visible window first (instant results)
2. Background thread continues full file scan
3. Results stream in progressively
4. Cancel on new query

### Thread Communication
- `tokio::sync::mpsc`: File watcher → Parser (async)
- `std::sync::mpsc`: Parser → GUI (sync)
- `Arc<Mutex<AppState>>`: Shared state across threads

### Format Auto-Detection
Heuristics:
1. First line is JSON → JSON parser
2. Timestamp pattern → Syslog parser
3. Laravel pattern → Laravel parser
4. Fallback → Plain text

## Performance Targets
- File open: <50ms for 1GB files
- Line iteration: >1M lines/sec
- Search: <100ms for 100MB files
- Memory overhead: <50MB + mmap
- Follow mode latency: <100ms from file write

## Sciter Setup Requirements
**macOS**:
1. Download Sciter SDK from sciter.com
2. Extract to `/usr/local/sciter-sdk/` or similar
3. Add to PATH: `export SCITER_SDK=/usr/local/sciter-sdk`
4. Copy `bin.osx/libsciter.dylib` to system library path or bundle with app

**Linux**:
```bash
sudo apt-get install libgtk-3-dev
# Download and setup Sciter SDK similar to macOS
```

## Error Handling Strategy
- File not found → Show error dialog with file picker
- Permission denied → Show error with sudo hint
- File >10GB → Confirmation dialog before proceeding
- Invalid regex → Highlight syntax error in search box
- Watcher errors → Disable follow mode, show notification

## Future Enhancements (Out of Scope)
- Multiple file tabs
- Export filtered results
- Custom parser plugins
- Remote log streaming (SSH/HTTP)
- Log aggregation from multiple files
- Bookmarks
- Split view comparison

---

**Next Steps**: Execute this plan to create a performant log viewer that can handle multi-GB files with a responsive GUI and real-time tailing capabilities.

title: Jake UX/DX Improvement Recommendations
content:
# Jake UX/DX Improvement Recommendations

## Executive Summary

Jake is a well-designed command runner with excellent documentation. The following recommendations focus on reducing friction, improving discoverability, and fixing inconsistencies that could confuse users.

---

## 1. CLI UX Improvements

### 1.1 Missing `jake init` Command
**Issue**: Users must manually create a Jakefile from scratch.
**Recommendation**: Add `jake init` that scaffolds a starter Jakefile, ideally with project-type detection (Node, Go, Rust, etc.).

### 1.2 No Recipe Name Autocomplete/Suggestions
**Issue**: If user types `jake buld` (typo), they get "Recipe not found" with no suggestion.
**Recommendation**: Add fuzzy matching suggestions like:
```
error: Recipe 'buld' not found
Did you mean: build?
Run 'jake --list' to see available recipes.
```

### 1.3 `--list` Output Could Be More Scannable
**Issue**: `--list` shows good info but for large Jakefiles, it's dense.
**Recommendation**:
- Add `--list --short` for just recipe names (one per line, pipeable)
- Consider tree-style output for grouped recipes

### 1.4 No Way to See Recipe Details
**Issue**: Can't inspect a recipe without reading the Jakefile.
**Recommendation**: Add `jake --show <recipe>` to display the recipe definition with dependencies, commands, and metadata.

### 1.5 Watch Mode UX
**Issue**: `-w` without pattern watches "everything" which may not be obvious.
**Recommendation**: When entering watch mode with no pattern, print what's being watched:
```
Watching: src/**/*.ts, Jakefile
Press Ctrl+C to stop
```

---

## 2. Error Messages & Diagnostics

### 2.1 Parse Errors Lack Context
**Issue**: Parse errors show line/column but not the actual line content.
**Recommendation**: Show the offending line with a caret pointing to the error:
```
error at line 5, column 12: expected ':', found 'ident'
  5 | task build name
    |            ^^^^
```

### 2.2 Dependency Cycle Errors
**Issue**: "Cyclic dependency detected in 'X'" doesn't show the full cycle.
**Recommendation**: Show the cycle path:
```
error: Cyclic dependency detected
  build -> test -> lint -> build
```

### 2.3 `home()` Function Failure
**Issue**: When `$HOME` is undefined and there's no passwd fallback, what happens?
**Recommendation**: Error explicitly with a clear message:
```
error: home() failed - $HOME is not set
  hint: Set HOME environment variable or ensure user entry exists in /etc/passwd
```

### 2.4 @needs with Custom Hint Format
**Issue**: `@needs docker "Install from docker.com"` - the quote parsing might be unclear.
**Recommendation**: Document this syntax prominently and consider alternative syntax like `@needs docker -> "hint"` for clarity.

---

## 3. DSL Clarity & Consistency

### 3.1 `@quiet` vs `@silent` vs `@` Prefix
**Issue**: There are multiple ways to suppress output:
- `@quiet` on recipe (suppresses command echo)
- `@` prefix on command (suppresses that command's echo)
- Planned `@silent` (suppress all output)

**Recommendation**: Document the difference clearly in GUIDE.md with a comparison table.

### 3.2 Task vs File vs Simple Recipe Distinction
**Issue**: Three recipe syntaxes (`task X:`, `file X: deps`, `X:`) might confuse newcomers.
**Recommendation**: Add a decision tree in docs:
```
Should I use task, file, or simple recipe?
- Need file dependency tracking? → file
- Always runs, clear intent? → task
- Quick & simple (Make-style)? → simple
```

### 3.3 `@cd` vs `@workdir`
**Issue**: `@cd` exists, but TODO mentions `@workdir` as planned. These seem identical.
**Recommendation**: Decide on one. `@cd` is more intuitive for shell users.

### 3.4 Directive Naming: `@only-os` Hyphenation
**Issue**: `@only-os` uses a hyphen while other directives don't (`@dotenv`, `@require`).
**Recommendation**: Consider `@os` or `@platform` for consistency, or document the reason.

### 3.5 Hook Naming: `@pre`/`@post` vs `@before`/`@after`
**Issue**: Both exist. Are they aliases or different features?
**Recommendation**: Pick one pair and make the other an alias (or remove). Document which is canonical.

---

## 4. Documentation Gaps

### 4.1 Variable Scoping Rules
**Issue**: When are variables available? Recipe scope vs global scope vs exported to shell?
**Recommendation**: Add a "Variable Scoping" section explaining:
- Global variables (defined at top level)
- Recipe parameters
- `@export` behavior (currently broken per TODO.md)
- Shell variable access (`$VAR` vs `{{VAR}}`)

### 4.2 Function Return on Error
**Issue**: What do functions like `home()`, `extension()` return on invalid input?
**Recommendation**: Document error behavior for each function.

### 4.3 Parallel Execution Limitations
**Issue**: Known bug - parallel execution doesn't handle `@each`, `@if`, etc.
**Recommendation**: Add a warning in docs: "Note: `-j` parallel mode currently doesn't support recipes with directives like @each or @if."

### 4.4 Import Precedence
**Issue**: If two imports define the same recipe name (without namespacing), which wins?
**Recommendation**: Document conflict resolution rules.

---

## 5. Feature Discoverability

### 5.1 No Built-in Examples
**Issue**: `samples/` directory is great but users must find the repo.
**Recommendation**: Add `jake --examples` that prints common patterns or links to docs.

### 5.2 Hidden Features Not Discoverable
**Issue**: Features like `$1`/`$2`/`$@` positional args, `{{func()}}` syntax aren't obvious from `--help`.
**Recommendation**: Add "See GUIDE.md for full documentation" to help output, or a `jake --cheatsheet` command.

### 5.3 Shell Completions Missing
**Issue**: Tab completion would significantly improve UX.
**Recommendation**: This is already planned in TODO.md - prioritize it.

---

## 6. Known Bugs Impacting UX (from TODO.md)

| Bug | User Impact | Priority |
|-----|-------------|----------|
| Parallel executor ignores directives | `-j` silently breaks complex recipes | High |
| `@export` not working | Confusing: variables work in Jake but not shell | High |

---

## 7. Quick Wins (Low Effort, High Impact)

1. **Typo suggestions** for recipe names (Levenshtein distance)
2. **`--list --short`** for pipeable output
3. **Document @quiet vs @ prefix** difference
4. **Warn about parallel limitations** in --help or when `-j` used with directives
5. **Print watch patterns** when entering watch mode

---

## 8. Medium-Term Recommendations

1. **`jake init`** command with templates
2. **`jake --show <recipe>`** to inspect recipes
3. **Shell completions** (bash/zsh/fish)
4. **Better parse error display** with source context
5. **VS Code extension** for syntax highlighting (already planned)

---

## Summary: Top 5 Priorities

1. **Fix parallel executor directive handling** - Silent breakage is worse than failure
2. **Add typo suggestions** for recipe names - Quick win, big UX improvement
3. **Shell completions** - Table stakes for CLI tools
4. **Document variable scoping** - Common source of confusion
5. **`jake init`** - Reduces friction for new users

title: Jake E2E Sample Scripts & Test Plan
content:
# Jake E2E Sample Scripts & Test Plan

## Goal
Create comprehensive sample Jakefiles in `samples/` that exercise all implemented features, plus an E2E test system using **jake to test jake** (dogfooding).

## Design Decisions
- **Test Runner**: Jake tests Jake - `samples/Jakefile` runs all E2E tests
- **File Creation**: Real files - actually create temp files to test globs, staleness
- **Output Matching**: Pattern matching - use grep patterns, not exact comparison

---

## Sample Directory Structure

```
samples/
├── Jakefile                    # Master test runner (jake tests jake)
├── 01-basics/
│   ├── Jakefile               # Variables, deps, params, default recipe
│   └── patterns.txt           # grep patterns for expected output
├── 02-parallel/
│   ├── Jakefile               # 4 independent tasks for -j4 testing
│   └── patterns.txt
├── 03-imports/
│   ├── Jakefile               # Main file importing modules
│   ├── lib/
│   │   ├── build.jake         # @import "lib/build.jake"
│   │   └── deploy.jake        # @import "lib/deploy.jake" as deploy
│   └── patterns.txt
├── 04-hooks/
│   ├── Jakefile               # Global @pre/@post + recipe hooks
│   └── patterns.txt
├── 05-file-targets/
│   ├── Jakefile               # file recipes with globs
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── main.ts
│   │   ├── utils.ts
│   │   └── lib/
│   │       └── helper.ts
│   └── patterns.txt
├── 06-environment/
│   ├── Jakefile               # @dotenv, @export, $VAR, ${VAR}
│   ├── .env
│   ├── .env.local
│   └── patterns.txt
├── 07-conditionals/
│   ├── Jakefile               # @if env(), exists(), eq(), @elif, @else
│   └── patterns.txt
└── 08-full-project/
    ├── Jakefile               # All features combined - realistic project
    ├── lib/
    │   ├── common.jake
    │   └── docker.jake
    ├── src/
    │   ├── app.ts
    │   └── config.ts
    ├── .env
    └── patterns.txt
```

---

## Files to Create

### 1. `samples/Jakefile` - Master Test Runner
```jake
# Jake E2E Test Suite - Jake testing Jake

version = "0.1.0"

@default
task test-all: [test-basics, test-parallel, test-imports, test-hooks,
                test-files, test-env, test-conditionals, test-full]
    echo "All E2E tests passed!"

task test-basics:
    @pre echo "[TEST] 01-basics"
    cd 01-basics && ../../zig-out/bin/jake 2>&1 | grep -f patterns.txt
    @post echo "[PASS] 01-basics"

task test-parallel:
    @pre echo "[TEST] 02-parallel"
    cd 02-parallel && ../../zig-out/bin/jake -j4 all 2>&1 | grep -f patterns.txt
    @post echo "[PASS] 02-parallel"

# ... similar for each test directory
```

### 2. `samples/01-basics/Jakefile`
```jake
# Test: Basic features - variables, dependencies, parameters

greeting = "Hello"
target = "World"

@default
task hello:
    echo "{{greeting}}, {{target}}!"

task build:
    echo "Building..."

task test: [build]
    echo "Testing after build"

task greet name="Developer":
    echo "Welcome, {{name}}!"

task all: [hello, build, test]
    echo "All done!"
```

### 3. `samples/02-parallel/Jakefile`
```jake
# Test: Parallel execution with -j flag

task compile-frontend:
    echo "Compiling frontend..."
    sleep 0.1
    echo "Frontend done"

task compile-backend:
    echo "Compiling backend..."
    sleep 0.1
    echo "Backend done"

task compile-worker:
    echo "Compiling worker..."
    sleep 0.1
    echo "Worker done"

task compile-cli:
    echo "Compiling CLI..."
    sleep 0.1
    echo "CLI done"

@default
task all: [compile-frontend, compile-backend, compile-worker, compile-cli]
    echo "All compilations complete"
```

### 4. `samples/03-imports/Jakefile`
```jake
# Test: Import system

@import "lib/build.jake"
@import "lib/deploy.jake" as deploy

@default
task all: [compile, deploy.production]
    echo "Build and deploy complete"
```

### 5. `samples/03-imports/lib/build.jake`
```jake
task compile:
    echo "Compiling project..."

task lint:
    echo "Linting code..."
```

### 6. `samples/03-imports/lib/deploy.jake`
```jake
env = "staging"

task staging:
    echo "Deploying to {{env}}..."

task production:
    echo "Deploying to production..."
```

### 7. `samples/04-hooks/Jakefile`
```jake
# Test: Pre/post hooks (global and recipe-level)

@pre echo "[GLOBAL PRE] Starting jake..."
@post echo "[GLOBAL POST] Jake finished!"

task build:
    @pre echo "[RECIPE PRE] Preparing build..."
    echo "Building..."
    @post echo "[RECIPE POST] Build cleanup..."

@default
task deploy: [build]
    @pre echo "[RECIPE PRE] Preparing deploy..."
    echo "Deploying..."
    @post echo "[RECIPE POST] Deploy notification sent"
```

### 8. `samples/05-file-targets/Jakefile`
```jake
# Test: File targets with glob patterns

file dist/bundle.js: src/**/*.ts
    echo "Bundling TypeScript files..."
    cat src/*.ts src/**/*.ts > dist/bundle.js 2>/dev/null || touch dist/bundle.js
    echo "Bundle created"

file dist/app.min.js: dist/bundle.js
    echo "Minifying bundle..."
    cp dist/bundle.js dist/app.min.js
    echo "Minified"

@default
task build: [dist/app.min.js]
    echo "Build complete"

task clean:
    rm -rf dist/
    echo "Cleaned"
```

### 9. `samples/06-environment/Jakefile`
```jake
# Test: Environment variables

@dotenv
@dotenv ".env.local"
@export BUILD_MODE=production

task show-env:
    echo "API_URL: $API_URL"
    echo "DB_HOST: ${DB_HOST}"
    echo "BUILD_MODE: $BUILD_MODE"

@default
task deploy:
    @if env(CI)
        echo "Running in CI environment"
    @else
        echo "Running locally"
    @end
    echo "Deploying with API_URL=$API_URL"
```

### 10. `samples/07-conditionals/Jakefile`
```jake
# Test: Conditional logic

task check-env:
    @if env(CI)
        echo "CI mode enabled"
    @elif env(DEBUG)
        echo "Debug mode enabled"
    @else
        echo "Normal mode"
    @end

task check-files:
    @if exists(src/config.ts)
        echo "Config exists"
    @else
        echo "No config found"
    @end

@default
task install:
    @if eq($BUILD_MODE, "production")
        echo "Installing production dependencies"
    @elif eq($BUILD_MODE, "development")
        echo "Installing dev dependencies"
    @else
        echo "Installing all dependencies"
    @end
```

### 11. `samples/08-full-project/Jakefile`
Full realistic project combining ALL features - see implementation.

---

## Pattern Files (patterns.txt)

Each directory has a `patterns.txt` with grep patterns:

**01-basics/patterns.txt:**
```
Hello, World!
Building...
Testing after build
All done!
```

**02-parallel/patterns.txt:**
```
Compiling frontend
Compiling backend
Frontend done
Backend done
All compilations complete
```

---

## Implementation Steps

1. Create `samples/` directory structure
2. Create individual sample Jakefiles (01-08)
3. Create supporting files (lib/, src/, .env)
4. Create pattern files for each sample
5. Create master `samples/Jakefile` test runner
6. Test the full suite: `cd samples && jake test-all`

---

## Critical Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `samples/Jakefile` | Master E2E test runner |
| `samples/08-full-project/Jakefile` | Complex integration test |
| `samples/*/patterns.txt` | Expected output patterns |

title: Jake Future Features - Documentation Update
content:
# Jake Future Features - Documentation Update

## Task
Add detailed future feature ideas to TODO.md as reference documentation for potential future implementation.

## File to Modify
- `TODO.md` - Add expanded "Future Features" section with brainstormed designs

## Overview
Document four future features with design details:

---

## 1. Remote Cache Support

### Problem Statement
Currently, jake's cache is local (`.jake/cache`). In CI/CD or team environments, each machine rebuilds from scratch even when inputs haven't changed globally.

### Current Architecture
- SHA256 content hashing in `src/cache.zig`
- Storage: `.jake/cache` (plaintext: `path\0hash\0mtime\n`)
- Interface: `load()`, `save()`, `isStale()`, `updateHash()`

### Proposed Design

**Option A: HTTP Backend (Recommended)**
```jake
@cache-server "https://cache.example.com/jake"
@cache-auth env(JAKE_CACHE_TOKEN)

file dist/bundle.js: src/**/*.ts
    @cache inputs   # Push/pull from remote
    esbuild src/index.ts --bundle -o dist/bundle.js
```

Pros:
- Simple to self-host (any HTTP server with PUT/GET)
- Works with existing CDNs (Cloudflare R2, nginx)
- Authentication via headers

**Option B: S3-Compatible Backend**
```jake
@cache-backend s3
@cache-bucket "my-jake-cache"
@cache-region "us-east-1"

file dist/app: src/**/*.go
    go build -o dist/app
```

Pros:
- Native cloud integration
- Versioning/lifecycle policies built-in

**Option C: Content-Addressable Storage (CAS)**
```jake
@cache-backend cas
@cache-server "https://cache.example.com"

# Outputs stored by hash of (recipe + inputs hash)
file dist/bundle.js: src/**/*.ts
    esbuild src/index.ts --bundle -o dist/bundle.js
```

Key insight: Store outputs by `sha256(recipe_commands + input_hashes)`

### Implementation Approach

1. **Abstract cache backend** (`src/cache_backend.zig`):
```zig
const CacheBackend = union(enum) {
    local: LocalCache,
    http: HttpCache,
    s3: S3Cache,
};

pub const CacheInterface = struct {
    loadFn: fn (self: *@This(), key: []const u8) ?[]const u8,
    saveFn: fn (self: *@This(), key: []const u8, data: []const u8) !void,
    existsFn: fn (self: *@This(), key: []const u8) bool,
};
```

2. **Cache key generation**:
   - Key = `sha256(recipe_name + sorted_input_hashes + command_text)`
   - Stored value = tarball/zip of outputs

3. **Fallback strategy**:
   - Try remote → fall back to local → execute recipe
   - Upload to remote after successful local execution

### Syntax Options
```jake
# Global configuration
@cache-backend http "https://cache.example.com"
@cache-backend s3 bucket="jake-cache" region="us-east-1"
@cache-fallback local  # Fallback if remote unavailable

# Per-recipe opt-in
file dist/bundle.js: src/**/*.ts
    @remote-cache      # Enable remote caching for this recipe
    esbuild ...
```

### Considerations
- **Security**: Signed URLs, auth tokens, read-only vs read-write
- **Bandwidth**: Compress outputs before upload
- **TTL**: Auto-expire old cache entries
- **Invalidation**: Manual purge command (`jake --purge-cache`)

---

## 2. Container Execution (@container)

### Problem Statement
Recipes often need specific tool versions or isolated environments. Currently, users must pre-install dependencies or manually wrap commands in `docker run`.

### Use Cases
1. **Reproducible builds**: Same container = same output
2. **Isolated dependencies**: Node 18 for one task, Node 20 for another
3. **Cross-compilation**: Build Linux binaries on macOS
4. **Security**: Untrusted code in sandboxed environment

### Proposed Design

**Basic Syntax**
```jake
task build:
    @container node:20-alpine
    npm install
    npm run build
```

Equivalent to: `docker run -v $(pwd):/work -w /work node:20-alpine sh -c "npm install && npm run build"`

**Advanced Options**
```jake
task build:
    @container image="rust:1.75" mount="./src:/src:ro" env="CARGO_HOME=/cache"
    @container volumes="cache-vol:/cache"
    @container network=host
    cargo build --release

# Or multi-line for clarity
task test:
    @container begin
        image: python:3.12
        mount: ./tests:/tests:ro
        mount: ./src:/src:ro
        env: PYTHONPATH=/src
        workdir: /tests
    @container end
    pytest
```

**Named container definitions**
```jake
@define-container rust-builder
    image: rust:1.75
    mount: ./:/work
    mount: cargo-cache:/usr/local/cargo
    workdir: /work

task build:
    @container rust-builder
    cargo build --release
```

### Container Runtime Detection
```zig
const ContainerRuntime = enum {
    docker,
    podman,
    nerdctl,
    none,
};

fn detectRuntime() ContainerRuntime {
    // Check in order: podman, docker, nerdctl
    // Return first available
}
```

### Implementation Approach

1. **Parse @container directive** in parser.zig:
   - Extract image, mounts, env vars, network settings
   - Store in `Recipe.container_config: ?ContainerConfig`

2. **Modify runCommand()** in executor.zig:
   - If recipe has container config, wrap command
   - Build docker/podman command line
   - Handle volume mounts (pwd → /work by default)

3. **Volume handling**:
   - Auto-mount current directory as `/work`
   - Support named volumes for caching
   - Read-only mounts for source protection

4. **Environment forwarding**:
   - Forward @export variables to container
   - Support container-specific env vars

### Syntax Variants Considered

```jake
# Option 1: Directive-based (recommended)
task build:
    @container node:20
    npm run build

# Option 2: Recipe attribute
task build @container="node:20":
    npm run build

# Option 3: Indented block
task build:
    @in node:20
        npm install
        npm run build
    @end

# Option 4: Special recipe type
container build using node:20:
    npm run build
```

### Edge Cases
- **Nested containers**: Error or flatten?
- **Interactive prompts**: Pass through TTY (`-it` flag)
- **Cache directories**: Named volumes for node_modules, cargo cache
- **Exit codes**: Propagate container exit code
- **Signals**: Forward SIGINT/SIGTERM to container

---

## 3. Workspace/Monorepo Support

### Problem Statement
Large codebases split into packages need coordinated builds. Currently requires manual imports or wrapper scripts.

### Use Cases
1. **Monorepo builds**: Build all packages in dependency order
2. **Selective execution**: Only rebuild changed packages
3. **Shared configuration**: Common settings across packages
4. **Package discovery**: Auto-find packages by pattern

### Proposed Design

**Root Jakefile**
```jake
@workspace packages/*
@workspace apps/*
@workspace-order topological  # or: parallel, sequential

# Shared variables available to all packages
version = "2.0.0"
node_version = "20"

# Run across all packages
task build:
    @workspace-run build

task test:
    @workspace-run test --parallel

task lint:
    @workspace-run lint --parallel --continue-on-error
```

**Package Jakefile** (`packages/core/Jakefile`)
```jake
# Inherits variables from root
# Can declare dependencies on other packages

@package-deps utils, common

task build:
    echo "Building core v{{version}}"
    npm run build

task test: [build]
    npm test
```

### Workspace Commands
```bash
jake build                    # Build all packages in order
jake build --package=core     # Build specific package
jake build --changed          # Only changed packages (git diff)
jake build --since=main       # Changed since branch
jake test --parallel          # Run tests in parallel across packages
jake --list-packages          # Show discovered packages
```

### Implementation Approach

1. **Package discovery** (`src/workspace.zig`):
```zig
const Package = struct {
    name: []const u8,
    path: []const u8,
    jakefile: *Jakefile,
    dependencies: [][]const u8,
};

fn discoverPackages(patterns: []const []const u8) ![]Package {
    // Glob expand patterns
    // Load each Jakefile
    // Parse @package-deps
    // Return sorted by dependencies
}
```

2. **Dependency resolution**:
   - Build package dependency graph
   - Topological sort for build order
   - Detect circular dependencies

3. **Execution modes**:
   - Sequential: One package at a time
   - Parallel: All independent packages together
   - Topological: Respect inter-package deps

4. **Change detection**:
   - Git diff to find changed files
   - Map files → packages
   - Include downstream dependents

### Syntax Options

```jake
# Option 1: Glob-based (recommended)
@workspace packages/*
@workspace apps/*

# Option 2: Explicit list
@workspace packages/core, packages/utils, apps/web

# Option 3: Config file
@workspace-config workspace.json

# Option 4: Convention-based
# Auto-discover any directory with Jakefile
@workspace-discover
```

### Advanced Features

**Filtering**
```jake
task deploy:
    @workspace-run deploy --filter="apps/*" --exclude="apps/internal"
```

**Shared recipes**
```jake
# Root Jakefile
@workspace-recipe lint
    eslint .

# All packages get this recipe automatically
```

**Package-specific overrides**
```jake
# packages/legacy/Jakefile
@override lint
    # Different linter for legacy code
    jshint .
```

---

## 4. Built-in Recipes

### Problem Statement
Common tasks (docker build, npm scripts, git operations) require boilerplate. Built-ins provide tested, optimized implementations.

### Use Cases
1. **Reduce boilerplate**: `@builtin docker` vs 20 lines of Jakefile
2. **Best practices**: Built-ins follow recommended patterns
3. **Discoverability**: `jake --list-builtins` shows available recipes
4. **Customization**: Override or extend built-in behavior

### Proposed Design

**Usage Syntax**
```jake
@builtin docker
@builtin npm
@builtin git

# Now available:
# jake docker:build
# jake docker:push
# jake npm:install
# jake npm:test
# jake git:commit
# jake git:release
```

**Customization**
```jake
@builtin docker
    registry = "ghcr.io/myorg"
    image_name = "myapp"

# Override specific recipe
task docker:build:
    @description "Custom build with extra args"
    docker build --build-arg VERSION={{version}} -t {{image_name}} .
```

### Built-in Catalog

**@builtin docker**
```jake
# Auto-generated recipes:
task docker:build:
    @description "Build Docker image"
    docker build -t {{docker.image}}:{{docker.tag}} .

task docker:push: [docker:build]
    @description "Push to registry"
    docker push {{docker.image}}:{{docker.tag}}

task docker:run:
    @description "Run container locally"
    docker run -it --rm {{docker.image}}:{{docker.tag}}

# Variables with defaults:
docker.image = env(DOCKER_IMAGE, "app")
docker.tag = env(DOCKER_TAG, "latest")
docker.registry = env(DOCKER_REGISTRY, "docker.io")
```

**@builtin npm**
```jake
task npm:install:
    @description "Install dependencies"
    @cache package-lock.json
    npm ci

task npm:build: [npm:install]
    @description "Build project"
    npm run build

task npm:test: [npm:install]
    @description "Run tests"
    npm test

task npm:lint:
    @description "Run linter"
    npm run lint --if-present
```

**@builtin git**
```jake
task git:commit message:
    @description "Stage and commit changes"
    git add -A
    git commit -m "{{message}}"

task git:release version:
    @description "Create release tag"
    git tag -a v{{version}} -m "Release {{version}}"
    git push origin v{{version}}

task git:changelog:
    @description "Generate changelog"
    git log --oneline $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD
```

**@builtin go**
```jake
task go:build:
    @description "Build Go binary"
    go build -o dist/{{go.binary}} ./cmd/{{go.binary}}

task go:test:
    @description "Run tests with coverage"
    go test -cover ./...

task go:lint:
    @description "Run golangci-lint"
    golangci-lint run
```

**@builtin rust**
```jake
task rust:build:
    cargo build --release

task rust:test:
    cargo test

task rust:clippy:
    cargo clippy -- -D warnings
```

### Implementation Approach

1. **Built-in storage**: Embed recipes in binary or load from `~/.jake/builtins/`

2. **Parser integration**:
```zig
fn parseBuiltin(name: []const u8, config: ?[]const u8) ![]Recipe {
    const builtin_source = builtins.get(name) orelse return error.UnknownBuiltin;
    // Parse builtin source
    // Apply config overrides
    // Return recipes with prefixed names
}
```

3. **Override mechanism**:
   - User recipes with same name take precedence
   - `@extend` keyword to wrap built-in

4. **Discovery**:
   - `jake --list-builtins` - Show all available
   - `jake --show-builtin docker` - Show source

### Extensibility

**User-defined builtins**
```jake
# ~/.jake/builtins/mycompany.jake
task mycompany:deploy env:
    @description "Deploy to company infrastructure"
    kubectl apply -f k8s/{{env}}/
```

```jake
# Project Jakefile
@builtin mycompany

task deploy: [build, mycompany:deploy env=production]
```

---

## Priority & Dependencies

| Feature | Complexity | Dependencies | Value |
|---------|------------|--------------|-------|
| Built-in Recipes | Medium | None | High (immediate usability) |
| Remote Cache | High | Cache abstraction | High (CI/CD value) |
| Container Execution | Medium | Executor refactor | Medium |
| Workspace/Monorepo | High | Import system | Medium (niche use case) |

### Suggested Implementation Order
1. **Built-in Recipes** - Foundation for others, standalone value
2. **Remote Cache** - High value for teams/CI
3. **Container Execution** - Enables reproducible builds
4. **Workspace Support** - Most complex, specialized need

---

## Action
Document these in TODO.md as "Future Feature Ideas" with enough detail to serve as design reference when implementation begins later.

## What to Add to TODO.md
Replace the brief "Future Features (Lower Priority)" section with expanded documentation including:
- Problem statement for each feature
- Proposed syntax examples
- Implementation notes (key files, approach)
- Design decisions (HTTP+S3, auto-detect runtimes, embedded+user builtins)

title: Recipe List Filtering Feature
content:
# Plan: Recipe List Filtering Feature

## Research Summary

### What Other Tools Do

| Tool | List Command | Group Support | Pattern Filtering |
|------|--------------|---------------|-------------------|
| **just** | `--list`, `--groups` | `[group('name')]` attribute, groups shown in list | None built-in |
| **Taskfile** | `--list`, `--list-all` | None | None (relies on `--json` + external tools) |
| **Rake** | `rake -T [pattern]` | None | Prefix pattern: `rake -T db` shows db:* tasks |
| **Make** | None built-in | None | None |

**Key insights:**
- **Rake's approach** is the most elegant: `rake -T db` filters to tasks starting with "db"
- **just** separates concerns: `--groups` to list groups, `--list` shows all grouped
- No tool combines group + pattern filtering in one command

### Jake's Current State (from exploration)

- `recipe.group` field already exists and is used
- `--list` already groups output visually
- `--list --short` outputs one name per line (scriptable)
- `--summary` outputs space-separated names (for completions)
- Private recipes (starting with `_`) are already filtered out

---

## Three Proposed Approaches

### Approach 1: Explicit Separate Flags (Most Explicit)

```bash
jake --list --group build      # Filter to group "build"
jake --list --filter 'test*'   # Glob pattern on recipe names
jake --list --group dev --filter '*test*'  # Combined
jake --list --groups           # List available group names only
```

**Flag names considered:**
- `--group` / `-g` - Filter by group name (matches existing `recipe.group`)
- `--filter` / `-F` - Pattern filter (avoids confusion with `-f` for file)
- `--groups` - List groups only (like `just --groups`)

**Pros:**
- Very explicit, no ambiguity
- Easy to document and discover
- Matches just's `--groups` for listing groups
- `--filter` with glob is familiar (Git, find, etc.)

**Cons:**
- Verbose for simple cases
- Two different flags to remember

**Implementation:**
```zig
// In args.zig
.{ .short = 'g', .long = "group", .value = "GROUP", .desc = "Filter recipes by group" },
.{ .short = 'F', .long = "filter", .value = "PATTERN", .desc = "Filter recipes by glob pattern" },
.{ .short = null, .long = "groups", .desc = "List available groups" },
```

---

### Approach 2: Positional Argument with Smart Detection (Most Concise)

```bash
jake --list build      # Group name (exact match) or pattern
jake --list 'test*'    # Contains glob chars → pattern match
jake --list            # No filter → all recipes
```

**Detection logic:**
1. If arg contains `*`, `?`, `[` → treat as glob pattern
2. Else → try exact group match first, then prefix match on recipe names
3. Ambiguity resolution: groups take precedence (more intentional)

**Pros:**
- Very concise for common cases
- Follows Rake's ergonomic pattern
- Natural to type

**Cons:**
- Ambiguous: is `build` a group or recipe filter?
- Harder to explain behavior
- What if group name contains glob chars?

**Variation 2b: Prefix syntax for groups**
```bash
jake --list @build     # @ prefix → group filter
jake --list test*      # No prefix → pattern on names
jake --list            # All recipes
```

---

### Approach 3: Unified `--match` Flag with Type Prefix (Balanced)

```bash
jake --list --match 'group:build'    # Filter by group
jake --list --match 'name:test*'     # Filter by name pattern
jake --list --match 'test*'          # Default: name pattern
jake --list --match 'group:*'        # List all groups (wildcard)
```

**Pros:**
- Single flag to remember
- Extensible (could add `type:task`, `alias:*`, etc.)
- Explicit about what's being matched

**Cons:**
- More typing for simple cases
- Colon syntax may feel unusual
- `group:*` for listing groups is awkward

---

## Final Decision

**Approach 1 (Explicit Separate Flags)** - User approved.

**Flags (no short flags for clarity):**
- `--group GROUP` - Filter to recipes in GROUP
- `--filter PATTERN` - Filter recipe names by glob pattern
- `--groups` - List available group names

**Output modes:**
- `jake --list --group build` → Normal grouped output, filtered
- `jake --list --short --group build` → One per line, filtered
- `jake --groups` → One group per line

---

## Files to Modify

1. `src/args.zig` - Add new flags: `group`, `filter`, `groups`
2. `src/executor.zig` - Modify `listRecipes()` to accept filter params
3. `src/main.zig` - Wire up new flags to executor
4. `src/glob.zig` - Reuse existing glob matching for pattern filter
5. `TODO.md` - Add feature documentation

---

## TODO.md Addition (Final)

Add this to the "### CLI Improvements" section under "## UX/DX Improvements":

```markdown
5. **`--list` filtering** (Planned)
   - [ ] `--group GROUP` - Filter recipes to specified group
     - `jake --list --group build` shows only recipes in "build" group
     - Works with `--short`: `jake --list --group build --short`
     - Case-sensitive exact match on `recipe.group`
   - [ ] `--filter PATTERN` - Filter recipes by glob pattern
     - `jake --list --filter 'test*'` shows recipes starting with "test"
     - `jake --list --filter '*lint*'` shows recipes containing "lint"
     - Reuses existing `glob.zig` pattern matching
     - Matches against recipe name (not aliases)
   - [ ] `--groups` - List available group names
     - `jake --groups` outputs one group name per line
     - Sorted alphabetically, no duplicates
   - [ ] Combined filtering: `jake --list --group dev --filter '*test*'`
   - [ ] Error handling: `--group nonexistent` warns "No recipes in group 'nonexistent'"

   **Research**: [just](https://just.systems/man/en/listing-available-recipes.html) uses `--groups` to list groups. [Rake](https://batsov.com/articles/2012/03/08/ruby-tip-number-2-get-a-list-of-all-rake-tasks/) uses `rake -T pattern` for prefix filtering. [Taskfile](https://taskfile.dev/docs/reference/cli) relies on `--json` + external tools.
```

title: Unified `lira` CLI Tool
content:
# Plan: Unified `lira` CLI Tool

Create a new `lira` CLI that combines compiler and VM functionality into one convenient tool.

## Overview

- **New crate:** `crates/lira/` (binary-only, no lib.rs)
- **Commands:** `run`, `compile`, `check`, `repl`
- **Approach:** Thin wrapper using existing `lirac` and `liravm` library APIs (no code duplication)

## Files to Create/Modify

| File | Action |
|------|--------|
| `Cargo.toml` | Add `"crates/lira"` to workspace members |
| `crates/lira/Cargo.toml` | New - package config with dependencies |
| `crates/lira/src/main.rs` | New - CLI entry point with all commands |
| `justfile` | Update `run` recipe to use unified CLI |

## Implementation Steps

### 1. Create crate structure

**`crates/lira/Cargo.toml`:**
```toml
[package]
name = "lira"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
description = "Lira programming language CLI"

[[bin]]
name = "lira"
path = "src/main.rs"

[dependencies]
lirac = { path = "../lirac" }
liravm = { path = "../liravm" }
```

### 2. Implement commands in `main.rs`

**Command implementations (all reuse existing APIs):**

```rust
// run: compile in-memory + execute (no temp files)
fn run_command(file: &str) -> Result<i32, String> {
    let source = fs::read_to_string(file)?;
    let bytecode = lirac::compile_with_imports(file, &source)?;
    liravm::run(&bytecode)
}

// compile: delegates to lirac::compile_file()
fn compile_command(input: &str, output: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    lirac::compile_file(input, output)
}

// check: delegates to lirac::check_file()
fn check_command(file: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
    lirac::check_file(file)
}
```

**REPL implementation:**
- Read-eval-print loop with `> ` prompt
- Track brace depth for multi-line blocks (`.. ` continuation prompt)
- Wrap input in `fn __repl_main() { ... }` and execute
- Special commands: `:quit`, `:help`
- Limitation: no persistent variables between statements (document this)

### 3. CLI structure

```
lira run <file.li>              # Compile and execute
lira compile <file.li> [-o out] # Compile to bytecode
lira check <file.li>            # Type check only
lira repl                       # Interactive REPL
lira --help | --version
```

### 4. Update justfile

```just
run file:
    cargo build --package lira --release
    ./target/release/lira run {{ file }}
```

## Key Patterns to Follow

**Compile + run pattern** (from `crates/lirac/tests/integration.rs:47-58`):
```rust
let source = fs::read_to_string(source_path)?;
let bytecode = lirac::compile_with_imports(source_path, &source)?;
liravm::run(&bytecode)
```

**Argument parsing** (manual, matching existing tools - no clap dependency)

## Notes

- Existing `lirac` and `liravm` binaries remain for backwards compatibility
- No external CLI library needed - keeps dependencies minimal
- REPL is stateless (each statement compiles independently)
